name: Muhamed Isabegovic
title: Staff Engineer
summary: I make software and lead the teams that make it, and have for ten years. Lately that means AI features in hiring software and data pipelines with AI agents; before that, SaaS products in Ruby on Rails and trading systems in C++. I work with agents writing the code and engineers reviewing it, and I build open-source tools that keep that code reliable.

experience.title: Staff Engineer and Founder
experience.summary: My own company. Since 2025 I have worked through it on B2B contracts as a staff engineer and technical lead. It also runs my product Usput.ba and RubyConf Austria, and it ran EuRuKo 2024 while I was at Meisterlabs. The work is grouped below.

experience.title: A data platform with AI agents, from proof of concept to production
experience.summary: As staff engineer, working inside a client's team through an engineering consultancy.
bullets: Took over a proof-of-concept data platform with AI agents and, with my team, brought it to stable production, with observability for its pipelines and agents. Worked inside the client's team and helped set its technical direction.
Built the data pipelines on Azure and Microsoft Fabric in a medallion architecture: PySpark notebooks combine the sources, and knowledge graphs in FalkorDB are built on the result.

Built AI agents on OpenAI models in Microsoft Foundry that enrich and classify the data. They make fast, typed decisions through OpenAI's Decisions API and reach the graph and the data as tools through MCP servers.
Introduced AI-native delivery in my team: agents write the code; engineers shape the work and review the result. Helped the client's engineers bring AI into their own development lifecycle.

experience.title: AI features in hiring software
experience.summary: As AI product developer for a large applicant tracking system, on Rails and Ember.js.
bullets: Owned AI features from pitch and spec to rollout and measurement, working in Shape Up.

Shipped a feature that requests missing information to all customers: it detects what an application is missing, drafts a short questionnaire for the candidate with an LLM, saves the answers to the application and re-runs screening.

Rebuilt AI screening on the product's trigger system, so recruiters can screen at any stage and save criteria on job templates. Backfilled every company and rolled it out to all customers behind Flipper feature flags.

Moved the prompts for the AI features into Langfuse, with datasets, LLM judges and live scoring of production traffic. Ran A/B experiments there between prompt and model versions and promoted the winners.

Shipped a customer-requested feature that moves candidates automatically according to the screening outcome. Made screening wait for CV parsing, so no candidate is screened before their CV has been read.

experience.title: Consulting for an early-stage speech-to-text product
experience.summary: AI work, architecture review, and product vision with the founder.

experience.title: Technical lead through an acquisition
experience.summary: At a seed-stage AI startup in recruiting, acquired shortly after I joined.
bullets: Led two teams, one on our Rails product and one on the acquirer's Node.js/TypeScript product, and owned delivery jointly with a product manager.

Merged the two products after the acquisition: a single Vue.js frontend, one shared database for clients and login sessions, and common ATS integrations, with new functionality shipped behind Flipper flags.
Co-built and maintained the event-driven system on Redis Pub/Sub that connects the two stacks and that new functionality is built on, with Google Cloud Tasks as a fallback and to manage workload.

Built the data pipelines that import jobs, candidates and applications from 20+ applicant tracking systems, normalise them into one model and pass them on to the AI features. The AI features worked the same for every client, and adding a new ATS needed no new code elsewhere.
Introduced spec-driven development: features are written up as specs and agreed first, then implemented with coding agents and reviewed by engineers.

Owned DevOps and CI/CD on Google Cloud, including monitoring and observability for the parts my teams ran. Ran integration and background jobs on Google Cloud Functions, triggered by events, queues or a schedule.

experience.title: Founder and AI Engineer
experience.summary: A travel guide to Bosnia and Herzegovina with thousands of visits a month, which I build and run alone on Rails and Hotwire, deployed with Kamal. It is where I first try AI features with real users, behind Flipper flags.
bullets: Built retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on pgvector: descriptions, audio-tour scripts and itineraries are written from records retrieved from a places API and the site's own database, not from the model's memory.
Built the LLM layer on RubyLLM with schema-enforced structured output, layered retries, JSON repair and versioned prompts, configured for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini models.
Wrote an MCP server in plain Ruby, with tests and a rule-based validator that catches invented details in the records the model creates.

experience.title: Conference organiser
experience.at: EuRuKo 2024; founder of RubyConf Austria and GoatConf
bullets: EuRuKo 2024, Sarajevo: 3 days, 3 tracks, 50 speakers from 25+ countries, 700 attendees.
RubyConf Austria 2026, Vienna: 13 speakers and ~200 attendees, with workshops and a community day built around a treasure hunt app I wrote (hunt.rubyconf.at).
Led EuRuKo 2024 and RubyConf Austria 2026 end to end, budget and sponsorships included, with a small volunteer team. GoatConf follows in Tuzla in June 2027.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
experience.summary: Maker of MindMeister and MeisterTask. I worked on MindMeister and the accounts system, in Rails and React, with MySQL and Sidekiq.
bullets: Proposed, designed and built a plans and permissions system shared by Accounts, MindMeister and MeisterTask. It replaced feature checks hardcoded across the apps, so the product team could set up plans and run billing experiments without developer time.

Built MindMeister product features for three years, behind Flipper feature flags, and ran A/B experiments across markets: pricing and plans, paywalls and upgrade prompts, onboarding and sign-up, and new features before release.

Maintained, monitored and expanded the Kubernetes setup for MindMeister: its dashboards, metrics and alerts, the Helm charts and deployment configuration, and new services and environments. Split backend and frontend deployments into separate pipelines, so the frontend went from weekly releases tied to the backend to daily ones.

experience.title: Engineering Manager
experience.summary: An ATS for tech and data-science hiring: three Ember.js apps on a Ruby on Rails monolith, with PostgreSQL on Kubernetes. I had joined as a junior engineer in 2016 and returned to lead engineering.
bullets: Led the engineering team as it grew from about 12 to about 30 engineers across backend, frontend and DevOps, fully remote across seven time zones. I reported to the founders.
Formed an architecture committee; its members became the tech leads I trusted to shape the work and lead delivery.

Stayed hands-on: built core backend features and the recruiter and candidate dashboards, reviewed code, and worked on the API between the Ember.js apps and the Rails monolith, framework upgrades, database and performance, and on infrastructure and CI/CD with the DevOps engineer.
Agreed priorities, timelines and trade-offs with the founders, product, design and sales, and ran sprint, roadmap and release planning, retrospectives and the rules for code review.
Designed the hiring process and, for the engineers I hired, ran the technical interviews, made the decisions and onboarded them.

experience.title: C++ Software Engineer
bullets: Built trading algorithms and worked on the traders' analytics platform, in C++ on a real-time actor-model system (C++ Actor Framework).
Built a Python test environment that emulated markets and trading systems, to test algorithms without live markets.

open_source.name: empty-shell
open_source.text: A starting repository for projects run with a coding agent: rules, checks and an empty wiki, with enola, tabula and taha inside.

open_source.name: enola
open_source.text: Checks a codebase against its architecture rules in CI. I built its rule system and maintain four Ruby gems for Rails teams.

open_source.name: tabula
open_source.text: A Rust tool that keeps a project's memory and decisions as plain files in git, and judges finished work against what was decided.

open_source.name: taha
open_source.text: Runs a coding agent unattended within a set mandate and returns finished, checked work.

open_source.name: enola-guides
open_source.text: Guides to enola for Rails, Ember.js, Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust, with a catalogue of 26 architecture laws. Ten releases since August 2026, on RubyGems, npm, PyPI and crates.io.

open_source.name: tended and pi-brain
open_source.text: Knowledge bases maintained by a coding agent, so that people and agents work from the same written specs and decisions. Published on PyPI (tended) and npm (pi-brain, ten releases).

open_source.name: treasure_hunt
open_source.text: A location-based treasure hunt for conferences, built on Rails 8.1 for RubyConf Austria 2026. MIT licence.

recommendations.text: I worked with Muhamed on the same team for a year, and he quickly became one of the people I relied on most. Muhamed leads by doing. When we hit a hard problem, he didn't start with a long discussion. He wrote the code, showed it working, and then we talked. That habit moved the team forward more than once. He is a strong Ruby on Rails engineer and a natural architect. He took on leading the technical direction and shaping the code, and his decisions held up as the project grew. No challenge was too big or too unfamiliar for him. He is resourceful and knowledgeable, and when the answer wasn't obvious, he knew where to look. He is precise and professional, and he holds a high bar. He is also direct. When something wasn't good enough, he said so plainly, even when that was hard to hear. It was always about the work and never about the person, and it made both our code and our team better. I would gladly work with Muhamed again, and I recommend him to any team that needs a Rails engineer who can lead.
recommendations.context: worked on my team for a year

recommendations.text: Muhamed is one of the most amazing professionals I have ever worked with. He is extremely talented, dependable, and disciplined. Moreover, he is always willing to push himself beyond limits to make a product successful. With Muhamed's excellent communication and engineering management skills everything is possible. At Experfy, Muhamed single-handedly managed the team collaboration consisting of 7+ timezones. He has a vast reservoir of talent - enabling him to lead Backend, Frontend, and DevOps teams with flying colors. In design thinking sessions, Muhamed played a vital role with his powerful insight about the product roadmap and technical knowledge. As an engineering manager, he always backed his team with full support. In addition to these Muhamed conducted extremely high-yielding Sprint retrospectives. He was always willing to go the extra mile to increase productivity and eliminate blockers. I would strongly recommend Muhamed and would love to work with him again.

The word that best describes Muhamed is 'visionary'. I had the pleasure of co-organising RubyConf Austria with him. For more than a year, I watched Muhamed take ideas that sounded wildly unreasonable and somehow make them a reality. His standard response was: 'Don't worry about it. It's going to be fine. We'll deal with it.' When things went wrong, Muhamed stayed calm, made a decision and got moving. He expected a great deal from himself while remaining patient and generous with everyone around him. His enthusiasm pushed the whole team to aim higher, and he was genuinely fun to work with. Muhamed is a kind and capable leader. I would gladly work with him again. I have merely learned to be careful when he begins a sentence with, 'I have an idea.'
